title: Mouse's First Day of School
author: Lauren Thompson

demand_candidate.rationale: Simple first-day concepts, school objects, colours, and shapes are highly picturable and suitable for emergent communicators and early SPED learners.

book_summary: Mouse hides inside a bright red backpack and ends up at school, where he explores a classroom full of blocks, toy cars, crayons, paints, hats, and a drum, discovering colors, letters, numbers, and finally making new friends. The book uses rhythmic, onomatopoeic phrases like 'Squiggle, scribble, dot crayons!' as Mouse moves from station to station in the classroom.

fringe_justifications.backpack: Mouse decides to hide inside a bright red backpack, which carries him to school and is the opening image of the whole story.
fringe_justifications.blocks: Blocks are the first station Mouse explores upon arriving in the classroom.
fringe_justifications.car: The page 'Vrim, vrum, vroom a car!' shows Mouse encountering a toy car, one of the book's signature sound-effect lines.
fringe_justifications.crayons: The line 'Squiggle, scribble, dot crayons!' has Mouse marching across the page carrying a big yellow crayon.
fringe_justifications.hat: The phrase 'Feathery, floppy, boppy hats!' describes a dress-up station with hats that Mouse discovers.
fringe_justifications.drum: The line 'Thump, boom, bump a drum!' describes Mouse finding a drum among the classroom instruments.
fringe_justifications.book: Books are among the classroom stations/wonders Mouse finds, per multiple plot summaries of the story.
fringe_justifications.puzzle: Puzzles are listed among the specific classroom items Mouse discovers on his exploration, alongside blocks and books.
fringe_justifications.snack: Snack time is one of the classroom wonders described in the story as Mouse explores the room.
fringe_justifications.friend: The story ends with Mouse finding new friends, described as 'best of all' in the publisher's summary of the ending.
fringe_justifications.paint: Kirkus notes Mouse finds tubes of paint at the paint station right after the blocks and toy car.

grounding_note: Confirmed via multiple sources (Amazon editorial review, Kirkus Reviews, Simon & Schuster publisher page, Bookroo, Brooklyn Public Library) that Mouse hides in a red backpack, ends up at a preschool/classroom, and encounters blocks, a toy car, crayons, paint, hats, a drum, books, puzzles, snacks, and friends. Kirkus and the Amazon editorial review both independently list the same sequence of classroom stations, giving high confidence in the specific object list.
